questions.title: Three springs at 90°
questions.summary: Mass hung from a double spring and a single spring meeting at 90°. Extensions p and q satisfy p²/4 + q² = g²m²/k², so a graph of (p²/4 + q²) against m² gives k.

xlsx.desc: Six sets of S₁, S₂ readings for m = 200–450 g. Process p, q, (p²/4 + q²) and m², then find k from the trendline.

questions.title: RC circuit: discharge and charging data
questions.summary: Capacitor charged through R₁ then discharged through R₂ while timing the current; an engineer's charging dataset is analysed (t₀, I₀, charge from area, τ from ln I graph); plan to compare ½CV² with the work done by the cell.

xlsx.desc: Discharge readings every 10 s. Practise ln I against t to get τ = R₂C.
A practice version of the engineer's datasetQ2b: 151 readings at 0.2 s intervals. Find t₀, I₀, Q (trapezium rule) and τ.

questions.title: Bent-wire torsion pendulum
questions.summary: A V-shaped wire carrying two bobs hangs from a rubber band and oscillates about a vertical axis. T = 2πC sin(θ/2)√(m/k): plot T against sin(θ/2) to find k; compare two wires using T = πL√z; plan an investigation into the number of loops.

xlsx.desc: θ and two 10-oscillation timings for six angles. Process T and sin(θ/2) and find k.

notes.text: Present results: each column heading has a quantity and a unit separated by a slash, e.g. S₁ / cm. Units never go in the body of the table.
Raw lengths to 0.1 cm (the rule precision). Calculated quantities to the same s.f. as the raw data or one more.
Aim for at least 6 values over the widest range the springs allow without over-stretching them.
Include an m² column. That is your x-variable in (d), and examiners like seeing it tabulated.
Write the trendline equation exactly as the spreadsheet gives it, with enough s.f. to read off the gradient.
Linearise: y = (p²/4 + q²), x = m². Then the gradient is g²/k² and the intercept should be ≈ 0.
Sketch: label both axes with quantity and unit, mark the points as crosses, and draw the line of best fit.
"Expected change": say both what changes (gradient ÷ 4) and what stays (straight line through the origin).
